ashley: Heads-up — saw p99 tail climb ~30ms after the http2 writev smallwrite tweak in the canary. Looks host-side: tokenization + micro-writes => kernel-selection oddness + kvcache thrash.

omar: Which profile do you have? perf/pprof output would help, and any kvcache hit-rate around the spike.

ashley: Quick slices from the canary perf dump (filtered):
```
writev_many -> copy_user_generic_unrolled + tokenize_one
net::http2::writev_small -> syscall_overhead (sched_yield)
kvcache.lookup -> L1-miss + hot-shard-hop
```
Not super formal but the pattern is small fragmented writes -> more syscalls -> different hot paths hit. Also requests get split so kvcache keys end up on different shards, increasing miss rate.

kai: Sounds like fragmentation. Smallwrites mean more syscalls, which pushes the service onto a different kernel hotpath and changes batching heuristics. Also if streaming chunker emits tiny frames we lose prefix locality for KV keys. Can we gate coalescing on payload size?

marco: I ran a quick A/B on a dedicated pool with SMALLWRITE_COALESCE=0 (disable coalescing) and the p99 improved ~22ms, aggregate qps unchanged. Suggest a two-step: 1) canary revert SMALLWRITE_COALESCE for 24h, 2) add heuristic: coalesce only when payload >= 4KB or when per-connection outstanding > 8.

ashley: Agree. Also adding a short sampling probe in the kernel-selection path to log which kernel variant was chosen + kvcache shard id would make postmortems way faster. We should add a unit test for streaming chunker to assert coalescing heuristics.

omar: I'll add a perf metric to kvcache (kvcache.shard_miss_rate.sample) and open a tiny PR to plumb SMALLWRITE_COALESCE env + the size threshold flag.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rolled SMALLWRITE_COALESCE=0 to canary pool at 1825552480 :shipit: 

kai: Nice. After a 6h bake let's capture p50/p90/p99 and kvcache hit-rate. If stable we can implement the payload-size heuristic and keep default conservative. :thumbsup:

marco: Filing the follow-up doc + checklist now (will include perf commands and the perf snippet ashley pasted).

ashley: Thanks — will grab traces after the bake and paste the detailed perf flame.
